assessments.reasoning: I independently retrieved and verified the exact bytes of ALGOL 68-R, in ALGOL 68 Implementation and inspected the cited passage (Printed p. 21 (physical PDF p. 37), opening and THE LANGUAGE). Page 21 calls 68-R a language based on ALGOL 68 and lists documented differences. Its other use of ALGOL 60 appears in the Mark 1 compiler description.

challenge.method: Check both possible parent readings, the compiler implementation language, and Technical Note 802’s separate RS project.
challenge.results: The explicit base language is ALGOL 68. A local ALGOL 60 dialect is the compiler’s implementation language. TN802’s later Revised Report-based compiler is a separate system.

limitations: This edge is the relation asserted by the authors for 68-R. It does not decide the exact unrevised base draft.
